provenance.pins: datasheet p.1 Marking and Polarity drawing (TO-252: G left, D tab/centre, S right)

designVerdict: SELECTED - the two channel switches (Q1, Q2), driven by the LM5069.
notes: Replaces the P-channel TM40P06D (C7422850). N-channel because the LM5069 charge pump drives the gate above the source, which is what made the high-side gate network unnecessary.
100 V against the SMAJ36CA 58.1 V clamp is 1.72x, where the 60 V P-FET sat at 1.03x - a margin this design twice called uncomfortable and twice failed to fix.
Rds(on) 9.5 mOhm max at Vgs 10 V (p.1), roughly 13.3 mOhm at Tj 100 C, so 0.079 W at the 2.43 A channel current. Lower loss AND higher voltage than the 60 V P-FET, at $0.39 against $0.40.

Publishes a real SOA family (Fig. 12 p.4) with 10 us / 100 us / 1 ms / 10 ms / DC curves. CORRECTION: the DC curve runs at CONSTANT POWER, passing through (100 V, 1 A), so at Vds 36 V it allows roughly 100 W - not the 0.6 A / 21 W a first reading claimed, which was out by 4.5x. Against the 39.8 W power limit that is 2.5x. The TM40P06D had only a DC line and no family, which is why its SOA was unverifiable.
RthJA 50 C/W on 1 in2 of 2 oz copper (p.1 note 2), so about 2.5 W at 25 C ambient. Steady state is not the binding constraint; the 18 W ramp is, and that is transient.
Datasheet lists "PD Charger V-BUS" as a typical application.

The SOA chart is annotated 'RATED TC=25 C Single' - a case-temperature rating. On this board R_thJA is 50 C/W, so 39.8 W is only survivable because the ramp is ~100 ms. The datasheet publishes no Z_thJA curve, so the junction rise during the ramp is bounded by the SOA curve but is NOT verifiable from this datasheet.
Quote 9.5 mOhm (the p.1 max at Vgs 10 V), not LCSC's 7.5 mOhm typical, in anything load-bearing.
